title: Structural Studies of Single-Atom Yb3+ Defects in CrI3 2D Ferromagnets Using Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Van der Waals magnets exhibiting two-dimensional magnetic ordering are promising candidates for manipulating the spin degree of freedom in quantum technologies [1]. The layered ferromagnetic chromium triiodide (CrI3) has generated special interest because the interlayer magnetic exchange in few layer CrI3 is dependent on the structural stacking order [2], suggesting a route to in situ spin switching using external pressure or other strain techniques. The crystals adopt the monoclinic structure type C2/m at high temperature with a phase transition occurring at 220 K [3]. CrI3 2D ferromagnet has been extensively studied previously, but the use of impurity doping to generate new properties in CrI3 and other 2D magnets has not been fully explored. In this context, recent studies have shown that Yb3+ can serve as a spin-bearing optical point defect in CrI3. Yb3+ in CrI3 experiences a large internal effective (exchange) field, pinning the Yb3+ spin to that of the lattice, making it sensitive to small external magnetic fields as well as spontaneous spin correlations. These features, combined with the narrow line emission of Yb3+, open possibilities for further experiments exploiting strong coupling between optical and magnetic properties in 2D materials [4].
